slides.say: A pen costs x credits. A notebook costs three credits more than a pen. How much do y pens and y notebooks cost altogether?
There are letters in the question and in the choices. That's a hint that we can plug in numbers. We'll solve it two ways, by plugging in numbers, and then the math way, building the expression.
Let's plug in numbers. We choose easy numbers, but not zero or one, because those often make different choices look the same. And a different number for each letter. So x is two, and y is three.
A pen costs x, two credits. A notebook costs three credits more, two plus three, five credits.
at: A notebook costs three credits more

slides.say: We buy y pens and y notebooks, so three of each. Three pens cost three times two, six. Three notebooks cost three times five, fifteen. And six plus fifteen is twenty-one.
at: Three pens cost three times two

slides.say: So the right choice must give twenty-one when x is two and y is three. Choice number one says two x y plus three. Two times two times three is twelve. Plus three, that's fifteen. Not twenty-one, so it's out.
Choice number two says y, times two x plus three. First we work out two x plus three. That's four plus three, seven. Then three times seven is twenty-one. It works, so we keep it.

Choice number three says y, times x plus three. x plus three is five, and three times five is fifteen. Out. Choice number four says two y, times x plus three. Two y is six, and six times five is thirty. Out.
at: and three times five is fifteen
and six times five is thirty

slides.say: Only choice number two gives twenty-one. If two choices had given twenty-one, we'd choose new numbers and test only those two. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way. We start again from the givens, and build the expression step by step. A pen costs x. A notebook costs three more, x plus three.
One pen and one notebook together cost x plus x plus three, which is two x plus three.
at: One pen and one notebook together

slides.say: We buy y pens and y notebooks. That's y pairs, with a pen and a notebook in each pair. So the cost is y, times two x plus three. That's choice number two.

Choice number one says two x y plus three. It's the trap, because it multiplies the two x by y, but adds the three only once. Every notebook costs three more, so the three is paid y times. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number one says two x y
